_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 3.4. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: KIM is a customer lawfully in a shop. She goes behind the staff-only counter and takes cash from the till. Which is correct?
options: Burglary – she entered part of a building as a trespasser and stole
Only theft – she was allowed in the shop
explanations: She was a trespasser in that part.

questions.scenario: TOM has general permission to visit his father's house. He enters at night intending to steal his father's television. Is he a trespasser?
options: No, he has permission to enter
Only if he breaks a window
Yes – entering for a purpose outside the permission makes him a trespasser
Only if his father is asleep
explanations: Correct: R v Jones and Smith (1976).

questions.scenario: For s. 9(1)(a), when must the intent exist?
options: At any time during the day

questions.scenario: Which ulterior intent is NOT included in s. 9(1)(a)?
A homeless man enters an empty house as a trespasser only to sleep. Inside, the owner returns and the man causes him GBH. Which is correct?
options: No burglary because he had no intent on entry
Burglary under s. 9(1)(b) – having entered as a trespasser he inflicted GBH

questions.scenario: Having entered a house as a trespasser, a man smashes a TV out of anger but takes nothing. Is this s. 9(1)(b)?
options: No – criminal damage is not one of the acts in s. 9(1)(b)
Only if the TV is expensive
explanations: Correct (criminal damage may be charged; (a) needs intent at entry).

questions.scenario: RYAN gets stuck in a window with his head and right arm inside a house. He could not have reached anything. Has he 'entered'?
options: No, he must be fully inside
Only if he had a tool
Yes – partial entry can be enough, even if he couldn't steal from that position

questions.scenario: A man leans through a broken shop window and rummages among goods, with his feet on the pavement. Has he entered?
options: Yes – an effective entry is enough (R v Brown (1985))
Only if the shop is open

questions.scenario: A family lives in a caravan on a site. While they are away for the day, a man breaks in and steals. Is the caravan a 'building'?
options: Yes – an inhabited vehicle is included even if nobody is there at the time (s. 9(4))
No, a caravan is a vehicle
Only if it has wheels removed

questions.scenario: A man enters a building as a trespasser intending to steal 'anything worth stealing'. Is this enough for s. 9(1)(a)?
options: No, he must intend to steal a specific item
Yes – conditional intent to steal is generally enough (⚠ check)

questions.scenario: What mental element is required as to being a trespasser?
options: Knowing or being reckless that he is entering without permission

questions.scenario: Burglary of a dwelling has a higher maximum sentence than burglary of other buildings. Which is correct (⚠ check)?
A man, having entered a garden shed as a trespasser, tries to steal a lawnmower but is disturbed. Which is correct?
options: s. 9(1)(b) – attempting to steal after entering as a trespasser

questions.scenario: A man enters a school as a trespasser intending to smash the computers. Which offence?
options: s. 9(1)(a) burglary (intent to do unlawful damage)
No offence until damage is done
explanations: Burglary is complete on entry with intent.

questions.scenario: Which statement about 'building' is correct?
options: Any structure including tents for one night
Ordinary meaning with some permanence, e.g. shops, sheds, garages

questions.scenario: A guest is invited to a party in the living room. He goes upstairs into a bedroom he was told not to enter and steals a watch. Is this burglary?
options: Yes – he may be a trespasser in that part of the building
Only if he broke a lock

questions.scenario: Under s. 9(1)(b), which of these acts after entering as a trespasser makes the offence?
A man reaches through a letterbox with a hooked rod to take car keys. Could this be an entry?
options: Only if his hand goes in
Possibly – using an instrument can amount to entry in some circumstances (⚠ check edition)

questions.scenario: Which offence was removed from s. 9 by the Sexual Offences Act 2003?
explanations: Correct (now trespass with intent to commit a sexual offence, SOA 2003 s. 63).

questions.scenario: Which is the key difference between s. 9(1)(a) and s. 9(1)(b)?
options: (a) focuses on intent at entry; (b) on what is done after entry
